newsitem.title: USA: MSRB mum on guidance to NASD on "pay-to-play".
newsitem.headline: MSRB mum on guidance to NASD on "pay-to-play".

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's top staffer said the panel does not plan to let industry in on any new guidance it gives NASD about when to grant exemptions under the board's "pay-to-play" rule.
"I don't think there's any additional information we need to provide," Christopher Taylor, executive director of MSRB, said.
"The dealer community should be concentrating on compliance" with the rule, he said.
Enacted in April 1994, the MSRB's rule G-37 bars municipal dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.

Mary Schapiro, president of the National Association of Securities Dealers new regulatory authority, NASD Regulation, Inc., said recently her group will grant exemptions under only two narrow circumstances until it gets clearer guidance from MSRB.
One circumstance is when a disgruntled employee makes a political contribution deliberately to trigger the two-year ban on business.
The other is when an employee inadvertently exceeds the "de minimis" exemption under the rule. That provision permits an employee to give up to $250 to a candidate in his or her voting district.

Taylor said, "We have constant communication with NASD. It is a close working relationship. At this point, the board hasn't felt there is anything necessary to inform the industry in terms of additional guidance," he said.
